title: Data Modeling Basics
description: Understanding PEGA data model, properties, and data structures for building robust applications
learning_objectives: Work with data pages and transforms

introduction.title: Understanding PEGA Data Model
introduction.text: Data modeling in PEGA is fundamental to building robust applications. This lesson covers how to design and implement data structures that support your business processes. Unlike traditional databases, PEGA uses a property-based data model that is flexible and business-friendly.

sections.title: What is Data Modeling in PEGA?
sections.content: Data modeling in PEGA involves defining the structure and relationships of data that your application will use. The PEGA data model is built around properties, which are individual data fields that can be combined to create complex data structures.

sections.title: Core Data Concepts
sections.content: Understanding these fundamental concepts is essential for effective data modeling in PEGA.

subsections.title: Properties
subsections.content: Individual data fields that store information. Properties are the building blocks of your data model.

subsections.title: Data Types
subsections.content: Define what kind of data a property can hold and how it behaves.

subsections.title: Complex Properties
subsections.content: Advanced property types for handling structured data.

types.name: Page Group

sections.title: Creating Properties
sections.content: Step-by-step guide to creating properties in your PEGA application.

steps.title: Access Data Model

steps.title: Define Property Details

Set whether the field is required

sections.title: Data Pages
sections.content: Data pages are reusable data structures that provide efficient data access and caching.

creation_steps.title: Configure Data Source
instructions: Choose data source type (Database, Service, etc.)
Set up data transformation if needed

sections.title: Data Validation
sections.content: Implementing validation rules to ensure data quality and integrity.

validation_types.description: Ensure mandatory fields are not empty
Ensure values fall within acceptable ranges

practices.description: Use clear, consistent naming for properties
guidelines: Use consistent prefixes for related properties

practices.description: Choose appropriate data types for optimal performance
guidelines: Use Integer for whole numbers, not Text
Consider data size and performance implications
Use Page Lists for repeating data
Keep property hierarchies shallow when possible
Use data pages for frequently accessed data
Consider database indexing for large datasets

mistakes.description: Creating too many small, fragmented data structures
mistakes.solution: Balance normalization with usability and performance

mistakes.description: Using different naming conventions across the application
mistakes.solution: Establish and follow consistent naming standards

mistakes.description: Not implementing proper data validation rules
mistakes.solution: Add validation at property and business rule levels

mistakes.description: Not considering data access patterns and volume
mistakes.solution: Design with performance and scalability in mind
